forecasts.question: Will AGI be developed before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Up 1pp to 26% on bullish capability signals. Greg Brockman (OpenAI) publicly stated they are '~80% of the way to AGI' — strongest framing yet from a frontier-lab leader. An Anthropic co-founder recalibrated to target full recursive self-improvement around 2028 (earlier than prior public anchors). Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview cleared the UK AISI's 32-step 'The Last Ones' corporate-network simulation (3/10 runs, 73% expert-task success); GPT-5.5 followed with 2/10 solves and 71.4% expert success three weeks later. State of AI: May 2026 (Air Street) describes the field as 'ASI Finals' with three viable labs. No formal AGI declaration yet, and the resolution window now stands at ~32 months.
forecasts.base_rate: ~25% aggregated from Metaculus, Kalshi and expert surveys for AGI by 2029
factors_up: Brockman '80% to AGI' framing from OpenAI president (+2pp)
Anthropic targeting recursive self-improvement by ~2028 (+2pp)
Claude Mythos and GPT-5.5 clearing AISI 'Last Ones' cybersecurity range (+1pp)
ASI Finals narrative — concentrated capability competition (+1pp)
factors_down: AGI definition still contested; resolution requires lab declaration or 3+ researcher endorsement (-3pp)
Resolution window narrowing to ~32 months (-2pp)
Hassabis and researcher-median timelines still >5 years (-1pp)
Lab-government friction (Anthropic Pentagon exclusion) raises declaration coordination risk (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether commercial pressure forces an early AGI declaration
Whether benchmark gains translate to sustained agentic deployment
How regulators respond if a lab declares first
update_triggers: Any frontier lab issues a formal AGI declaration
≥3 leading AI researchers publicly endorse AGI achievement
>15pp single-release jump on ARC-AGI-2 / Humanity's Last Exam

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 20%. McKinsey's planned 10% headcount cut (a 'few thousand' non-client roles, primarily back-office) continues to anchor the trajectory; LinkedIn Economic Graph data show ~25% of entry-level consulting/finance postings now require AI fluency (vs <5% two years ago). Junior leverage compression is visible across MBB and Big-4, with PwC, EY, KPMG, Accenture, Deloitte and Bain all having announced layoffs since 2023. 33% peak-to-trough by Dec 2030 still demands sustained sector-wide contraction — current cuts are concentrated in support functions, with client-facing teams not yet hit at scale. ~55 months to deadline.
forecasts.base_rate: ~15-20% — major industries rarely lose ≥30% of value or employment within five years absent an extreme shock
factors_up: McKinsey 10% cut now telegraphed publicly (+3pp)
PwC, EY, KPMG, Deloitte, Bain all in cutting phase (+2pp)
AI fluency now table-stakes in 25% of entry-level consulting postings (+2pp)
Anthropic CEO continuing 'unusually painful' job-disruption framing (+1pp)
factors_down: 33% threshold is severe; few precedents in modern sector history (-3pp)
Demand for AI-transformation advisory partially offsets disruption (-3pp)
Resolution requires 2+ credible analyses — could be contested (-2pp)
Current cuts concentrated in support roles, not client-facing pyramids (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether AI compresses billable hours rather than just headcount
How fast leverage models adapt vs. shrink
Whether the resolution criterion of 'primarily attributed to AI' is met
update_triggers: Big-3 strategy firm announces ≥20% client-facing cut
Combined Big-4/MBB revenue down ≥15% YoY for two consecutive years
FT/Economist analysis explicitly attributing ≥33% sector compression to AI

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 3% on the day of UK local elections (May 7 2026). Latest YouGov voting intention (4-5 May): Reform 25%, Labour 18%, Conservatives 17%, Greens 15%, Lib Dems 14%. Reform's national share is below its 31% January peak (partly drained by new right-flank Restore Britain party) but still leads. Pre-election projections: Reform on course to gain 1,000+ council seats and take Essex, Norfolk, Suffolk; Labour projected to lose 1,500–1,900 councillors from a 2,557 base (50–74% of defended seats); Conservatives projected to lose ~907 of 1,362 seats. ITV/Survation London poll has Labour 'under siege' even in metropolitan strongholds. Without a sharp Reform collapse and Labour recovery, Labour winning most seats at the next GE remains a very low-probability outcome.
forecasts.base_rate: ~5-10% — incumbent parties rarely recover from sub-20% mid-term polling to win most seats
factors_up: Reform's right flank fragmenting (Restore Britain) could split the vote (+2pp)
First-past-the-post efficiency could favour Labour in 4-way splits (+2pp)
Mid-term polls historically overstate insurgent strength (+1pp)
Long timeline to next GE (up to Aug 2029) allows recovery (+1pp)
factors_down: Labour 18% nationally vs Reform 25% — 7pp deficit (-3pp)
Local election projections imply 1,500-1,900 Labour councillor losses (-3pp)
Greens taking left-flank vote, especially in London (-2pp)
ITV London poll shows Labour weak even in metropolitan strongholds (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether Reform consolidates or fragments by 2029
Whether Labour's economic record stabilises before the GE
How tactical voting reshapes a fragmented field under FPTP
update_triggers: Labour returns to ≥25% in national polling for sustained period
Reform falls below 18% nationally
Major economic shock or government crisis

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 9%. KMT/TPP impeachment vote against President Lai set for May 19; Taiwan studying Middle East lessons to harden against blockade. US IC reaffirms PLA preparedness target 2027 (preparedness ≠ action). No mobilisation indicators, no crossing of declared red lines. ~44 months remain to deadline.

forecasts.question: Will UK annual CPI inflation fall below 2.0% for at least one month before 1 January 2027?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 1%. Bank of England April 2026 Monetary Policy Report (April 30) and exchange of letters confirm CPI at 3.3% in March 2026, projected to ease only to 3.1% in 2026 Q2 before rising back to 3.3% in Q3 — a 1.4pp upward revision from February's projection. Bank Rate held at 3.75% (April 29 8-1 vote, with one member voting to hike). Higher-for-longer energy prices (Middle East conflict feeding through) plus services-inflation persistence make a sub-2% monthly print before Dec 2026 essentially mechanically infeasible. ~8 months to deadline.
forecasts.base_rate: ~5% — base rate for inflation falling 1.3pp in eight months absent a recession is low; current BoE projections imply rising not falling inflation
factors_up: Energy price collapse if Middle East conflict de-escalates (+1pp)
Sharp recession could force disinflation (+1pp)
Sterling strength on monetary tightening could pull import prices (+0.5pp)
Statistical base effects in late 2026 (+0.5pp)
factors_down: BoE projects 3.1% Q2 rising to 3.3% Q3 (-3pp)
Bank Rate held with one member voting to hike (-2pp)
Services inflation sticky around 4-5% (-2pp)
Energy pass-through ongoing through 2026 (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Pace of energy-price normalisation
Whether labour-market slack opens before year-end

update_triggers: Sharp drop in oil/gas to pre-conflict levels
Major UK recession or labour-market collapse
BoE rate cuts of >100bp

forecasts.question: Will UK average annual real GDP growth exceed 1.5% across the 2030s (2030-2039)?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 42%. OBR March 2026 EFO continues to anchor: real GDP per person averaging 1.1% 2026-2030, productivity (TFP) picking up to ~1% in the medium term, labour-supply growth declining toward 0.5% by 2030 (lower migration, ageing). Headline real GDP lands ~1.5-1.6% across the late 2020s baseline. For the 2030-2039 mean to exceed 1.5%, productivity must hold OBR's medium-term path AND labour supply must not collapse against demographic ageing. AI-led upside (productivity at 1.5%+) brackets the YES case; a return to the post-GFC 0.5% productivity trend brackets NO. With Reform-leaning political trajectory now likely (May 7 locals confirming the realignment), policy mix on planning, immigration, EU trade and AI uptake is uncertain in both directions.
forecasts.base_rate: Base rate for UK 10-year real GDP growth >1.5% is ~40-50% based on post-1980 distributions; current outlook closer to 40%
factors_up: OBR medium-term productivity path of ~1% (+2pp)
AI adoption could lift productivity by 0.5-1pp (+3pp)
Planning reform momentum (+1pp)
Possible energy / housing supply easing (+1pp)
factors_down: Demographic ageing dragging labour supply (-3pp)
Political volatility (Reform-leaning trajectory) creates policy risk (-2pp)
Persistent productivity weakness since 2008 (-2pp)
Climate / fiscal headwinds in the 2030s (-2pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether AI productivity gains accrue to UK output rather than US capital
Pace of labour-supply decline
Future government policy on planning, migration, EU trade
update_triggers: Sustained UK productivity surprise of >0.5pp
Immigration policy shift materially altering labour-supply path
UK formal re-entry of EU single market / customs union
